samples.summary: New `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` truncation (code sliced to 80 chars) has no test
samples.evidence: `safeEnvelope` (formatter.ts:162) slices `body.error.code` to `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` (80). The new suite tests the message cap ('caps a huge `message` on the envelope path', upstream-error.test.ts:130) and the sibling drop (:139), but no test ever passes a code longer than 80 characters, so the truncation of the one field agents branch on is entirely unexercised — it could be removed, or slice the wrong length, with the suite still green.

samples.summary: Dot-segment guard is only tested on the synchronous id paths, never on the workspace-derived URLs where it throws asynchronously
samples.evidence: upstream-error.test.ts:554 ('refuses a dot segment') covers `deleteDocument('..')` and `getCell(...,'.')`, both of which call `seg` in a non-async method so the throw is synchronous. `seg` is also applied to `this.config.workspace` in the `base` getter (http-client.ts:108) and in `apiKeysUrl()` (:425); with a workspace of `.`/`..` the throw happens inside `async request()`/`requestUrl()` and surfaces as a rejected promise instead, and no test covers either that path or how a command reports it. The traversal test only uses workspace `'../../..'` and `'../../evil'`, which are not dot segments.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts 'request paths pin every id to one segment' block

samples.summary: `upstreamErrorJson`'s envelope bounding (message cap, HTML message, sibling drop) is untested; only the `forwardUpstreamError` side of `safeEnvelope` is
samples.evidence: The `upstreamErrorJson` describe block (upstream-error.test.ts:563-599) only asserts verbatim forwarding of a small envelope and the HTTP_ERROR replacement path. The caps that the import/upload/download commands now inherit through `safeEnvelope` (message >500 chars, `<html>` message, >4000-byte body) are asserted only through `forwardUpstreamError`, so a regression that skipped `safeEnvelope` on the `upstreamErrorJson` branch (e.g. reverting to `JSON.stringify(res.data)`) would keep every test green.

samples.summary: Pre-existing upload error test cannot distinguish the new HTTP_ERROR synthesis from a verbatim dump
samples.evidence: `makeClient(false)` (files-upload.test.ts:31) returns `{ error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }` — itself a valid envelope — and the test at :223 asserts only `err.join('')).toContain('HTTP_ERROR')`. That assertion holds under the old verbatim `JSON.stringify(res.data)` and under the new `upstreamErrorJson`, and would also hold if the body were forwarded unbounded, so it provides no coverage of the changed behavior in files/upload.ts:216. The new suite's 'files upload' case does cover it, so this is a weak-assertion note rather than a coverage hole.

samples.summary: Envelope with a `code` but no `message` is never exercised
samples.evidence: `safeEnvelope` only sets `error.message` when `'message' in body.error` (formatter.ts:164), so a `{error:{code:'X'}}` body is forwarded without a message. Every envelope fixture in the new suite (ENVELOPE at upstream-error.test.ts:31, the 'keeps extra fields' body at :69, the cap tests at :133/:143) carries a message, so this branch is untested.
searchedFor: read all envelope fixtures in packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts

finding.summary: api-keys URL/method/body are never asserted after the fetch→requestUrl rewrite
finding.evidence: `apiKeysUrl()` (http-client.ts:383-397) is new code: it rebuilds the management URL (`${server}/workspaces/${encodeURIComponent(workspace)}/api-keys`), now percent-encodes workspace and key id, and moves GET/POST/DELETE + the `{name}` body into `requestUrl`. Every test that touches these calls stubs fetch with `vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(...)` (upstream-error.test.ts:219-228 and 376-383) which returns the same response for ANY url/init, and the only assertion on fetch args is `retryHeaders.Authorization` (line 409-411). Nothing asserts the request URL, the HTTP method, or the POST body — so if the rewrite had pointed api-keys at `this.base` (`/api/v1/workspaces/...`), dropped the DELETE method, or lost the `{name}` payload, every test here would still pass while all three commands broke in production. Searched the whole cli package for `api-keys|apiKeysUrl|listApiKeys|createApiKey|revokeApiKey` and for `toHaveBeenCalledWith(` in packages/cli/test; no test pins these request arguments.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing assertions exist in the very file cited. packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:416-488 is a describe block 'api-keys requests keep their URL, method and body' that pins, against the real HttpClient with only global fetch stubbed: the management URL 'https://api.test/workspaces/ws-1/api-keys' (:444, :450, :459) — which would fail if api-keys were pointed at this.base '/api/v1/...'; the HTTP methods GET/POST/DELETE (:451, :460, :472); the POST body JSON.parse(init.body) toEqual { name: 'ci key' } plus the Content-Type header (:461-464); the DELETE key-id segment `${KEYS_URL}/key-1` (:471); and the percent-encoding of both a hostile workspace and a hostile key id, '..%2F..%2Fevil' and '..%2F..%2F..%2Fauth%2Flogout' (:477-486), matching seg() usage at packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:423-435. Assertions read fetchMock.mock.calls[0] arguments directly, so the reviewer's grep for 'toHaveBeenCalledWith(' would not have matched them; the 'api-keys' grep would have matched :420 and :444 in the current tree. Nothing under test is over-mocked — apiKeysUrl/requestUrl/seg all execute for real.
